title: A Stability Analysis of AdamW: Unstable Equilibria and Non-Convergence
claim: Even for a simple convex objective, the method's equilibrium exists yet its iterates fail to converge, oscillating persistently.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, shared equilibrium dashed line across panels
description: Three side-by-side line plots share a dashed vertical or horizontal marker at x*=0.495. The left panel shows a yellow parabola f(x)=(x-0.5)^2 with a red star at its minimum, labeled Equilibrium. The middle panel shows a blue implicit objective F(x). It has the same minimum and a red star, but it rises sharply and goes vertical at x=1. A grey hatched region to the right is labeled Divergent. The right panel plots the iterate x(T) in green against discrete steps from 0 to 2000. It starts near 0.8, dips, then oscillates around the dashed x* line with periodic spikes and never settles. Each panel has its own legend. The eye goes first to the green oscillating curve, which contrasts with the smooth convex curves on the left.
caption: AdamW with $\eta=10^{-2},\ \beta_1=0.99,\ \beta_2=0.9,\ \lambda=1,\ e=10^{-2}$. Left: quadratic objective $f(x)=(x-\tfrac{1}{2})^2$. Middle: implicit objective $F(x)$ whose stationary point coincides with AdamW’s equilibrium. Right: AdamW iterates $x(T)$ over time, showing non-convergence despite the simple convex objective.
abstract: AdamW is ubiquitous in deep learning, yet its behavior remains poorly understood. We analyze its dynamics through the lens of dynamical systems and show that AdamW admits an implicit fixed-point objective: its fixed points coincide with the stationary points of a constrained and regularized optimization problem. However, not all of these fixed points are stable under AdamW's dynamics, and stability depends sensitively on curvature, weight decay, and momentum parameters. Even in one-dimensional settings, equilibria may be unstable, and trajectories can exhibit persistent oscillations rather than convergence to them. We further extend the analysis to higher dimensions, deriving sufficient conditions for local stability of the continuous-time dynamics, and propose a convergent modification that preserves AdamW's fixed points. These results clarify what optimization problem AdamW is associated with, when its convergence can be expected, and how its dynamics could inspire more reliable optimizers.
